evidence_text: Management attributed the Q1 food-delivery margin decline to seasonal delivery-partner availability pressure from reverse migration and the start of rains, alongside annual salary increments.
analyst_use_or_question: Use as a seasonality control before interpreting Q1 margin changes as structural deterioration.

evidence_text: Management described affordability as the largest unlock for expanding food delivery, while noting a need to improve affordability without subsidies or degraded service quality.
analyst_use_or_question: Frames affordability as a strategic growth lever and creates a hypothesis about order growth versus contribution economics.

evidence_text: Bolt was described as a 10-minute option for selected fast-prep food items; One BLCK as faster delivery for premium subscribers; Snacc as functional meals/side-of-plate offerings; and 99-Store as single-serve fast-prep meals at ₹99.
analyst_use_or_question: Track each proposition separately; avoid attributing aggregate results to an individual initiative without specific causal evidence.

evidence_text: The letter describes priority assignment of delivery partners for selected orders and opt-in Ecosaver batching as operating capabilities supporting differentiated delivery propositions.
analyst_use_or_question: Potential mechanism for delivery-cost-per-order and utilisation changes; no quantified causal impact disclosed in this passage.

evidence_text: Instamart was positioned as a standalone brand with expanded non-grocery assortment; the letter says a large part of metro users had access to about 30,000 SKUs.
analyst_use_or_question: Supports the thesis that larger baskets and non-grocery mix are strategic drivers of AOV, not just price increases.

evidence_text: Management said the network built in H2 FY25 was being sweated, with selective additions for capacity bottlenecks or hyperlocal coverage rather than indiscriminate long-tail city expansion.
analyst_use_or_question: Relate growth and margin to capacity utilisation, store maturity, and density rather than store count alone.

evidence_text: Food delivery GOV was ₹8,086 crore, up 18.8% YoY; MTUs reached 16.3 million after adding 1.2 million in the quarter; adjusted EBITDA was ₹192 crore and 2.4% of GOV.
analyst_use_or_question: Benchmark growth and profitability; note source commentary attributes Q1 sequential margin movement partly to seasonality.

evidence_text: Quick-commerce GOV was ₹5,655 crore, up 107.6% YoY; AOV ₹612; contribution margin -4.6% of GOV; adjusted EBITDA margin -15.8%; darkstore area 4.3 million sq ft.
analyst_use_or_question: Rapid growth must be read with order economics and network investment; avoid interpreting GOV growth as profitability.

evidence_text: Out-of-home GOV was ₹1,056 crore; adjusted revenue ₹83 crore; contribution margin 4.4% of GOV; adjusted EBITDA ₹5 crore and 0.5% of GOV; active restaurant partners 41k.
analyst_use_or_question: Segment shows early profitable economics and a different margin structure from food delivery / quick commerce.

evidence_text: Management stated that total user cost of service (delivery fee, platform fee and membership cost) had remained around 5–6% of AOV over three years, while cost of delivery was around 12–13% of AOV.
analyst_use_or_question: A useful consumer affordability / platform monetisation lens; quote this as management-reported, not independently audited consumer-level data.
follow_up_or_validation: Find exact numerator, denominator and population definition before using as a KPI.

evidence_text: Management stated food advertising revenue was above 4% of GOV and larger than the segment adjusted EBITDA margin at that point; reported take-rate expansion was largely advertising-led.
analyst_use_or_question: Strong evidence that ad monetisation can support food-delivery economics without relying only on consumer fees or restaurant commission.

evidence_text: Bolt was available in 700+ cities and represented more than one-tenth of food orders; 99-Store was in 175+ cities; Deskeats covered 7,000+ tech parks across 30 cities; Food on Train covered 115+ stations.
analyst_use_or_question: Operational reach metrics can be used to contextualise growth initiatives; these are management-reported and should retain their exact as-of date.

evidence_text: Management attributed rising quick-commerce AOV to non-grocery selection and larger baskets; the disclosed non-grocery mix had expanded materially year over year.
analyst_use_or_question: Build a mix-versus-price decomposition if category mix data becomes available; current aggregate data cannot isolate the two.

evidence_text: Management stated average darkstore area was above 4,000 sq ft and that current order volumes were below estimated network capacity.
analyst_use_or_question: Use store area, orders/store/day and utilisation as a capacity-efficiency panel; avoid treating management capacity estimates as independently validated.

evidence_text: Management described Out-of-Home as an early-stage segment with strong growth, advertising revenue and improving profitability.
analyst_use_or_question: Separate advertising contribution from restaurant transaction economics when the letter discloses the relevant split.

evidence_text: Platform MTU was 22.9m (+34.0% YoY); consolidated adjusted revenue ₹5,911cr (+52.6%); B2C adjusted EBITDA margin -3.6% of B2C GOV; consolidated adjusted EBITDA loss ₹695cr.
analyst_use_or_question: Shows high growth alongside substantial group-level investment losses; segment profitability must not be confused with consolidated outcome.

evidence_text: Management said food GOV grew 18.8% YoY despite volatile consumption trends and higher-than-usual rainfall; double-digit order growth was the highest in two years.
analyst_use_or_question: Distinguish order-led growth from AOV-led growth; cross-check with order volume / AOV where series exist.

evidence_text: Instamart was positioned as an “Everything store”; Quick India Movement was a brand-partnered sale event; Maxxsaver was described as a cart-within-a-cart value proposition.
analyst_use_or_question: Potentially explains category expansion and basket-building, but promotions can have short-term unit-economic costs.

evidence_text: GOV ₹7,022cr (+107.6% YoY, +24.2% QoQ); AOV about ₹697 (+~40% YoY); NOV/GOV around 70%; contribution margin -2.6%; adjusted EBITDA loss ₹849cr.
analyst_use_or_question: One of the key episodes where rapid growth, improved basket metrics and materially negative EBITDA co-existed.

evidence_text: Swiggy said it does not publish Food Delivery or Out-of-Home NOV because discounts/subsidies are not structurally comparable in those businesses; it publishes GOV instead.
analyst_use_or_question: Critical design constraint: Food and OOH analysis should be GOV-based unless the source explicitly reports NOV. Do not synthesize a purported official NOV.
follow_up_or_validation: Capture exact Q&A wording and page in final evidence validation.

evidence_text: Management said food take rate was about 25.8%, up around 10bps QoQ, with much of the increase attributed to advertising; advertising was above 4% of GOV.
analyst_use_or_question: Treat 25.8% as a source-reported take-rate observation, not a value automatically reproducible as adjusted revenue/NOV.

evidence_text: Bolt had expanded to 700+ cities and more than one-tenth of food orders; 99-Store was present in 500+ cities and contributed a high-single-digit share of orders.
analyst_use_or_question: Useful adoption indicators; avoid assuming overlapping users or orders can be added across initiatives.

evidence_text: Non-grocery share of Instamart GOV was reported at 26.2%, versus 8.7% a year earlier; categories such as electronics, home and kitchen, and toys had increased their mix.
analyst_use_or_question: A direct mix mechanism for AOV expansion; ideal for a differentiated product-mix/average-basket research module.

evidence_text: Management reported a quick-commerce take rate of about 14.8%, down roughly 40bps QoQ, alongside NOV/GOV around 70%.
analyst_use_or_question: Shows trade-off between basket growth, discounting and monetisation; do not mechanically infer take rate from adjusted revenue/GOV.

evidence_text: The letter discussed around 1,102 stores across 128 cities, average store size around 4,160 sq ft and around 1,025 orders per store per day; management described substantial headroom versus capacity.
analyst_use_or_question: Support an operating-capacity model; compare cohorts/mature stores when available rather than just network-wide averages.

evidence_text: Management described expansion of quick-commerce while emphasising improved contribution economics, and highlighted investment in network footprint and assortment.
analyst_use_or_question: Use management’s stated capital-allocation priorities as qualitative context; specific capex attribution must be sourced to financial disclosures.

evidence_text: Food GOV was ₹8,959cr (+20.5% YoY); MTUs reached 18.1m (+22% YoY); adjusted EBITDA ₹272cr; adjusted EBITDA margin 3.0% of GOV.
analyst_use_or_question: Growth acceleration and margin expansion co-occurred; examine order growth, AOV and monetisation as possible contributors.

evidence_text: Quick-commerce GOV ₹7,938cr (+103.2% YoY); 34 net darkstores added to 1,136; darkstore area 4.8m sq ft; AOV ₹746; contribution margin -2.5%; adjusted EBITDA loss ₹908cr.
analyst_use_or_question: Scale expansion improved basket economics but losses remained substantial.

evidence_text: Management attributed food growth acceleration to order growth in the high teens, new speed/value/selection propositions and higher MTU growth; advertising and fleet utilisation were cited as margin drivers.
analyst_use_or_question: Hypotheses to test against available time-series metrics; avoid claiming causal attribution from quarterly aggregates alone.

evidence_text: Swiggy disclosed completion of a ₹10,000cr QIP in late December and a ₹2,400cr unlock from its Rapido stake sale, describing the balance sheet as strengthened.
analyst_use_or_question: Capital availability may explain investment capacity; include financing/capital events as context, not operating performance.

evidence_text: Bolt and 99-Store together represented more than one-fifth of food delivery volumes; Eat Right was described as around one in nine orders.
analyst_use_or_question: Potential product-mix proxy for growth initiatives; note proposition overlap and definition of order penetration.

evidence_text: Management stated contribution margin was about 7.6% of GOV and adjusted EBITDA margin about 3.0% of GOV, citing advertising and improved fleet utilisation.
analyst_use_or_question: Create a metric bridge only when source disclosures provide cost/revenue line items sufficient for a reconciled bridge.

evidence_text: Management discussed removing/culling low-AOV or unprofitable customers/orders and focusing on retention and quality users; it reported around 25% of stores were contribution-margin positive.
analyst_use_or_question: A rare unit-economics angle: growth quality, user cohorts, retention and store maturity rather than only aggregate GMV.

evidence_text: Management explained that more than 100bps of contribution-margin improvement was reinvested in customer fee waivers, limiting the reported sequential margin improvement.
analyst_use_or_question: A useful reinvestment-versus-margin analysis; separate gross underlying improvement from deliberate reinvestment where measurable.

evidence_text: The letter reported 25% of stores as contribution-margin positive and a top-decile store margin range of roughly 3–5%; mature cities were described as being around 3% contribution margin.
analyst_use_or_question: This can become a store-cohort economics module if later letters disclose consistent store-level distribution data.

evidence_text: Management described the Out-of-Home business as having reached profitability and continuing to scale with active restaurant partners and advertising monetisation.
analyst_use_or_question: Investigate whether scale, advertising or restaurant density best explains the transition; only disaggregate with disclosed data.

evidence_text: Food GOV grew 22.6% YoY, described as the highest since post-COVID demand normalised; management said the acceleration was driven more by order and user volumes than AOV.
analyst_use_or_question: Strong testable growth-quality claim. Compare order growth and AOV changes rather than only top-line growth.

evidence_text: Management described 99-Store, Snacc and Toing as affordability experiments; Snacc was shut down because expected steady-state category size did not justify incremental operational complexity.
analyst_use_or_question: Valuable product strategy lesson: explicit stop decisions and portfolio pruning can be analysed alongside launches.

evidence_text: Management characterised quick commerce as highly competitive and said it prioritised contribution-margin improvement and differentiated positioning over short-term headline growth.
analyst_use_or_question: Use as the management narrative behind slower order growth and improving unit economics; mark as management explanation, not independent causal proof.

evidence_text: Management said rapid delivery was becoming commoditised and that Instamart intended to compete through differentiated assortment and brand partnerships rather than price alone.
analyst_use_or_question: Potential differentiator thesis: assortment and retention as alternatives to discount-led growth.

evidence_text: Dineout GOV grew 43% YoY to ₹1,245cr; active monthly restaurant partners exceeded 52k; adjusted EBITDA margin reached 0.8%, supported by growing brand advertising revenue.
analyst_use_or_question: A distinct advertising-led, asset-light adjacent business; useful comparison with food delivery monetisation.

evidence_text: Management discussed food GOV growth of 22.6% YoY, MTUs up around 21%, orders up around 19%, and affordability/speed propositions contributing to adoption.
analyst_use_or_question: Cross-check growth drivers against source KPI charts; order-volume decomposition is especially important.

evidence_text: Management described food adjusted EBITDA margin at 3.3% of GOV and cited both contribution-margin improvement and operating leverage over the preceding two years.
analyst_use_or_question: Use a two-stage bridge: contribution margin to adjusted EBITDA, with any below-contribution cost data separately sourced.

evidence_text: Management said a no-fee-above-₹299 campaign ended in January 2026; contribution margin improved by about 450bps over the year, with March 2026 monthly contribution margin around -1.1%.
analyst_use_or_question: Important monthly-versus-quarterly distinction. Promotions and monthly run-rate should not be confused with quarter averages.

evidence_text: Management described reducing the share of unprofitable low-AOV customers/orders by roughly half and NOV/GOV improving from 68.7% to 72.0%.
analyst_use_or_question: Potential quality-of-growth metric; verify exact baseline dates and denominator before calculating deltas.

evidence_text: Management described the store network as able to support substantially more orders than then-current throughput; utilisation was around 40%, with top-decile store margins of 3–5%.
analyst_use_or_question: Build capacity slack and store maturity hypotheses; treat company-estimated capacity as management guidance.

evidence_text: Management stated Dineout crossed 52k average monthly active restaurant partners and that FY26 was its first full year of profitability.
analyst_use_or_question: Use to measure a segment’s path from growth to profitability.

evidence_text: At 31 March 2026 the letter reported consolidated cash balance of ₹15,053cr; quarterly capex was ₹188cr, primarily warehouse infrastructure and HQ relocation, with capex expected to decline in FY27.
analyst_use_or_question: Connect operating investment and liquidity context; separate cash balance, cash equivalents and reconciliation cash definitions.

evidence_text: Management stated the contribution-margin break-even milestone committed for Q1FY27 was achieved in May 2026; the quarter-average contribution margin was -0.2% of GOV.
analyst_use_or_question: Milestone refers to a month, not the full-quarter average; keep both facts in the data model.

evidence_text: Adjusted revenue per order was reported at ₹108, a sequential improvement of ₹11; adjusted EBITDA losses narrowed to ₹778cr.
analyst_use_or_question: RPO is a high-value monetisation KPI; preserve source definition and distinguish from take rate or AOV.

evidence_text: The company described partnerships with 400+ brands and a “Switch to Better” assortment initiative across 50 categories, contributing more than 15% of category sales.
analyst_use_or_question: A measurable mix-shift and differentiation thesis; later Q2FY27 claims should be treated as a subsequent expansion rather than identical denominator.

evidence_text: Food GOV grew 17.4% YoY; management said it would have been about 18% after normalising restaurant-driven cancellations linked to LPG supply constraints.
analyst_use_or_question: Store raw reported growth and the management-normalised figure separately; do not overwrite actual GOV growth.

evidence_text: Toing was available in 50 cities; management said two-thirds of new users were new to Swiggy or long-term dormant.
analyst_use_or_question: Potential incrementality signal; validate cohort definitions and avoid treating all Toing orders as incremental without counterfactual evidence.

evidence_text: Out-of-Home GOV was ₹1,529cr (+44.8% YoY), with 59k average monthly active restaurant partners and adjusted EBITDA margin of 0.9%.
analyst_use_or_question: Check whether growth and profitability persist when comparing subsequent quarter and annual results.

evidence_text: Management said more than 45% of stores were contribution-margin positive, 25% of stores were in a 3–5% contribution-margin range, and five of seven top cities were contribution-margin positive.
analyst_use_or_question: Strong candidate for a store-level maturity and distribution view; these are management-reported cut points, not full store-level data.

evidence_text: Management discussed removing more than four million unprofitable/low-quality users over three quarters and reported improving retention for newer user cohorts.
analyst_use_or_question: Useful growth-quality analysis, but cohort denominator and retention window must be explicitly captured.

evidence_text: Management described a path to adjusted EBITDA break-even at approximately ₹60,000cr annualised NOV, 25–30cr quarterly orders and around ₹30 contribution per order.
analyst_use_or_question: Translate into a driver-based bridge, but identify this as management’s target model, not FoodIQ’s independent forecast.

evidence_text: Management described the ₹30 contribution-per-order target through approximately ₹10 higher revenue/product mix, ₹10 advertising, ₹5 densification/automation and ₹5 operating leverage.
analyst_use_or_question: This is unusually rich evidence for a scenario model. Preserve the management bridge and test whether later disclosures support the individual levers.

evidence_text: Management described darkstore utilisation of about 40%, capacity for roughly twice current volume, and an expectation to add around 75 stores in Q2FY27.
analyst_use_or_question: Compare forecast store additions with reported net additions; distinguish gross openings, closures and net additions.

evidence_text: Management discussed a 49.5% fully diluted foreign shareholding cap and a potential approximately 80bps contribution-margin benefit following transition to an Indian Owned and Controlled entity.
analyst_use_or_question: Material business-model and working-capital catalyst; monitor regulatory completion and realised margin impact.

evidence_text: Management distinguished NOV from NRV and argued that NRV can include brand-funded discounts, advertising revenue and subscriptions in ways that may inflate apparent top-line versus consumer spend.
analyst_use_or_question: Capture NOV/NRV terminology and management position exactly; do not treat the comparison as a neutral accounting conclusion.

evidence_text: At its first Capital Markets Day on 6 August 2026, management set an FY31 aspiration of ₹10,000cr adjusted EBITDA, at GOV above ₹2.5 lakh crore and about 4% margins.
analyst_use_or_question: Treat as a long-term aspiration, not near-term guidance or a guaranteed forecast.

evidence_text: Quick-commerce NOV grew 13.4% QoQ to ₹6,594cr; orders rose 29.3% YoY to about 130m; 1.3m users were added; 69 net stores were added to reach 1,240.
analyst_use_or_question: Strong sequential acceleration, accompanied by increased investment and higher adjusted EBITDA losses.

evidence_text: Management described Switch brand partnerships (~400 brands), No!ce as present in one in eight baskets with around 15 percentage points higher retention, and Nectr as a curated produce offering.
analyst_use_or_question: Differentiation/retention mechanisms; preserve management-reported retention uplift as a comparison, not causal proof.

evidence_text: Management said shareholder approval for a 49.5% foreign shareholding cap was secured to qualify as Indian Owned and Controlled; inventory ownership transition was expected to complete over subsequent quarters, with a net margin benefit around 80bps.
analyst_use_or_question: Potential change in principal-versus-agent economics and working capital; scenario should include timing, inventory cost and working-capital sensitivity.

evidence_text: Food GOV grew 17.7% YoY to ₹10,054cr; September 2026 recorded more than 20% YoY growth; adjusted EBITDA reached ₹341cr and 3.4% of GOV.
analyst_use_or_question: A quarter may hide late-quarter acceleration; store monthly / intra-quarter data as a separate series from quarterly results.

evidence_text: Toing was in 50+ cities; two of every three new users were described as new to Swiggy or long-term dormant.
analyst_use_or_question: Useful customer acquisition signal; requires a clear definition of dormant and a cohort-based counterfactual for incremental lift.

evidence_text: Out-of-Home GOV was ₹1,508cr (+34.9% YoY); active restaurants reached 66k (+48% YoY); adjusted EBITDA positive for seven consecutive quarters; Dineout was in 80+ cities.
analyst_use_or_question: Segment-level consistency: quarterly active restaurants, geographic reach and margin trend.

evidence_text: Swiggy said over 50,000 delivery partners were enabled to file ITRs through the partner app; cumulative refund claims were ₹6.5cr and more than one-third filed for the first time.
analyst_use_or_question: A human-capital / ESG operating initiative; potential inclusion in responsible-platform assessment but not a direct financial KPI.

evidence_text: Instamart co-located battery swapping at last-mile stations; management said this could save partners up to 60 minutes daily and lower rental costs by up to 30%.
analyst_use_or_question: Potential delivery-partner productivity and cost-to-serve mechanism; figures are company-reported claims, not independent measured savings.

evidence_text: Platform MTU reached 27.8m (+21.0% YoY, +6.0% QoQ); B2C GOV ₹20,793cr (+24.6% YoY); consolidated adjusted revenue ₹7,909cr (+33.8%); consolidated adjusted EBITDA loss ₹760cr.
analyst_use_or_question: Use distinct B2C and consolidated scopes; the B2C GOV perimeter excludes Platform Innovations while consolidated revenue/EBITDA includes broader businesses.

evidence_text: Quick-commerce GOV ₹9,230cr (+31.4% YoY), NOV ₹6,594cr (+34.8% YoY), nAOV ₹506 (+4.3% YoY), contribution margin -1.0% of GOV, adjusted EBITDA loss ₹895cr.
analyst_use_or_question: Keep nAOV separate from the table’s AOV ₹708; they are different reported concepts and cannot be substituted.

evidence_text: The Q2FY27 historical KPI table shows Q1FY27 platform MTU at 26.2m, whereas the Q1FY27 letter’s own key-metrics table shows 27.5m.
analyst_use_or_question: Preserve both published values and attach a source conflict. The Q2FY27 MTU growth math is consistent with its displayed 26.2m history.
follow_up_or_validation: Ask whether this was a reclassification/restatement or an earlier reporting error; no note found on the KPI page.

evidence_text: Food take rate reached 26.1%, up 23bps YoY; management attributed monetisation growth to advertising; food adjusted EBITDA margin was 3.4% of GOV.
analyst_use_or_question: Potential comparison of platform monetisation and delivery cost efficiency, but take rate definition is source-reported and must not be guessed.

evidence_text: Management stated Bolt and 99-Store together represented more than 25% of food delivery volumes.
analyst_use_or_question: A sizeable share of volume comes from differentiated speed/affordability propositions; test if adoption correlates with order growth or cost-to-serve.

evidence_text: The chart reports 1,240 active darkstores, 1,192 orders per store per day, 5.21m sq ft active area and GOV per sq ft of ₹17,730.
analyst_use_or_question: Build store productivity ratios and trend them; distinguish period GOV/area from store-level profit and account for store openings/closures.

evidence_text: Dineout adjusted EBITDA margin was 0.5% of GOV in Q2FY27, after seven consecutive positive quarters; the prior quarter was 0.9%.
analyst_use_or_question: Tests sustainability and seasonality; profitability is sustained but quarterly margin can vary.

evidence_text: Platform Innovations adjusted revenue rose to ₹138cr and adjusted EBITDA loss was ₹162cr in Q2FY27.
analyst_use_or_question: Toing and other newer initiatives may sit outside B2C GOV while still affecting consolidated economics; avoid omitting them from group profit analysis.

evidence_text: Management reiterated 18–20% annual food delivery growth guidance excluding Toing; September had exceeded 20% YoY growth; food contribution margin was 7.7% of GOV and adjusted EBITDA margin 3.4%.
analyst_use_or_question: Guidance should be tracked on its stated ex-Toing basis; current quarter aggregate includes the reported business scope unless separated.

evidence_text: Management cited advertising monetisation, delivery density, shorter delivery distances and Bolt/99-Store as contributors to economics; those propositions represented over 25% of volumes.
analyst_use_or_question: Build a hypothesis map for margin expansion but do not allocate bps without disclosed cost bridge components.

evidence_text: Management said cross-users had about 25% higher combined frequency; repeat-user unit economics were positive in the oldest launch cities, while user-acquisition spending and scale sustainability remained under test.
analyst_use_or_question: Promising two-sided network/cross-sell module, but positive repeat-user economics do not establish full cohort or mature business profitability.

evidence_text: The letter referred to a GST Council proposal to change GST treatment for delivery services by unregistered persons from 18% to 5%; notification/implementation timing was not yet settled.
analyst_use_or_question: Store as a proposed regulatory change and scenario variable, not as an enacted or implemented change.
follow_up_or_validation: Subsequent government notification must be checked before changing assumptions.

evidence_text: Management described Steal Deals, QR digital menus with order/pay, in-seat cinema dining and Scenes event experiences as growth initiatives.
analyst_use_or_question: New monetisation use-cases can broaden transactions and advertising inventory; capture launch/coverage dates as they emerge.

evidence_text: Management described 1.3m user additions, month-one retention above 60% on average and platform frequency up 4.2% QoQ.
analyst_use_or_question: A differentiating growth-quality panel combines acquisition, retention and frequency, not only GOV.

evidence_text: Management attributed the 82bps QoQ contribution-margin decline to approximately -100bps targeted habit/dormant-user investments, -40bps user/category mix and +60bps operating leverage/efficiencies.
analyst_use_or_question: This is a rare disclosed driver bridge. Recreate it as management-attributed bps with exact rounding and reconcile to the reported -82bps.
follow_up_or_validation: Check arithmetic: -100 -40 +60 = -80bps; preserve the disclosed ~82bps delta and report ~2bps residual/rounding.

evidence_text: Management linked improved operating leverage to orders per store per day rising 9.5% to 1,192, alongside 69 net new stores; new stores can be underutilised for the first one or two quarters.
analyst_use_or_question: Use store additions and throughput jointly; model store maturity lag rather than assuming new capacity is immediately productive.

evidence_text: Management expected contribution margin in a zero to -100bps range in Q3FY27 and anticipated a roughly 100bps QoQ improvement in adjusted EBITDA margin.
analyst_use_or_question: Track both CM and Adj EBITDA margin separately; one is not a substitute for the other.

evidence_text: Management said Switch products generated over 20% of orders across more than 60 categories; No!ce was in more than one in eight orders across 500+ SKUs; Nectr launched in Bengaluru and one in six customers purchased it.
analyst_use_or_question: Potential measurable assortment/retention story; definitions and populations differ across initiatives and should not be pooled blindly.

evidence_text: Management described the transition starting mid-Q3FY27 over two to three quarters, an estimated 80bps margin benefit, an 8–10 day working-capital-cycle improvement and steady net working-capital days around 15.
analyst_use_or_question: Scenario model must couple margin benefit with inventory ownership, working capital and implementation timing.

evidence_text: Swiggy disclosed sale of its Lynks stake for about ₹500cr consideration and a separate ₹75cr primary investment for roughly 3.2% of Udaan; Lynks would no longer be reported from Q3FY27 and management expected about ₹20cr segment EBITDA improvement.
analyst_use_or_question: Create a structural break marker in Supply Chain trend series; do not interpret future improvement as purely operational.
follow_up_or_validation: Retain the transaction’s distinct sale proceeds and primary investment as separate cash-flow/equity events.
